I went to Jack Jack, a handmade burger restaurant near Anguk Station.
Personally, it was a place I was curious about after appearing in Black and White Chef.
The hip interior, reminiscent of an American handmade burger restaurant, had an impressive black and red color combination, and there were murals everywhere, creating a nice atmosphere. It has a 1st and 2nd floor structure, and you can see the kitchen on the way up to the 2nd floor, and I was impressed by how neatly it was maintained.

As expected from a handmade burger restaurant, the quality of the patties was good, and the Double Jack set had two beef patties and plenty of cheese, so I was satisfied. The Cajun fries were especially delicious with the flavor of chipotle sauce. The Magpie Kölsch beer had a soft, subtle honey flavor that went well with the burger.

Jack the Mac is a unique menu item containing mac and cheese and whole chicken breast. The chicken breast was very tender and juicy. Personally, I was a little disappointed, but it was a unique menu.
I recommend it to anyone who wants to enjoy handmade burgers in a nice atmosphere in Anguk.

reviews.text:
This review is based on my experience visiting last year.

- Sabe Jonggak - A sandwich brunch restaurant located in Jonggak. The sandwich was prepared like a meal. We created combinations that cannot be found on the market. You could see the ingredients being prepared and stir-fried right behind the stand.
1. Dark Rum Mont Blanc: A well-made croissant coated with dark rum syrup. A product that combines the subtle scent of dark rum, sweet syrup, and butter flavor.
2. Creme Brulee Butter Bar: A product where sugar is spread under the crust at the bottom of the butter bar and then charred with a torch. It had a flavor reminiscent of butterscotch and the caramelized bottom had a crunchy texture. The rich butter flavor covered the unique bright sweetness of creme brûlée, and the heavy sweetness was better than the pungent taste. The caramelization of the flavor was nice and harmonious.
3. Sleepy Joe: A sandwich made with mayonnaise sauce, cheddar cheese, red cabbage, minced vegetables, and beef on halal bread. The quality was significantly low compared to the price.
4. Button mushroom soup: Grind the button mushrooms to a line where particles can be recognized. It had a strong aroma of button mushrooms and a taste of garlic, and it had a rich texture. The flavor of liver and liver was generally strong, so it was disappointing that eating it with a sandwich killed the taste of the sandwich. The soup was great on its own, but it was a bit disappointing to eat it with cooked bread.

The unique combination of sandwiches was unique. Perhaps because it was busy during opening hours, the staff's response service was somewhat businesslike, which was disappointing.

The 'Chrysanthemums next to the fence' that I visited during my outing in Insa-dong was as neat and satisfying as I expected. In particular, I ordered the tangerine shaved ice and red bean shaved ice together, which are the representative menu items here. The charms of the two menus were clearly different, so it was fun to choose between them.

First of all, tangerine shaved ice is so refreshing and refreshing that it makes your eyes pop. Rather than having an artificial syrup taste, the natural sweet and sourness of the tangerine harmonized with the cool ice, making it perfect for cleaning your mouth cleanly after a meal. The red bean shaved ice that I ordered together was so delicious that I could immediately understand why this place is famous for its red beans. The red bean grains were alive and not crushed, but not too sweet, so you could feel the rich flavor, and even the chewy texture of the rice cake on top was perfect.

Thanks to the traditional-looking brassware, the temperature was maintained until the end, allowing us to enjoy the food coolly. The atmosphere in the store was also calm, making it great for casual conversation. I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to try authentic Korean desserts in Insa-dong.

A long time ago, my mother made a lot of kimbap every day to distribute to teachers, students, and neighbors, and the kimbap was always very popular. The owner says he personally goes to the market to find the best ingredients to create the taste he remembers.

If you want a new style of kimbap like cheese or tuna mayonnaise, you won't find it here. Instead, you can taste perfect, authentic kimbap, just like your grandmother used to make! There is a generous amount of seaweed, rice, pickled radish, stewed burdock root, spinach, carrots, crab meat, ham, fried egg, and fish cake. I came here after enjoying sweet and sour pork and fried rice in China, but I wanted to stop by at least one other store before going home, so I headed to Bruda Insa-dong branch, which caught my eye on the way to China.

The store is a renovated old building, so it has a certain charm. It only offers takeout, but you order through a kiosk, so after some deliberation, I ordered a medium iced Americano with an additional shot.

After waiting for a while to see if there was a backlog of orders, the iced Americano finally came out. I brought it out and took a sip. It wasn't the type with an emphasis on savory flavor or the acidity type that I like, but the price was good and I liked that it felt a little less common than the chain brands that appear a lot these days.

It wasn't particularly my type of taste, but it felt like an imported brand that wasn't found in Gangnam, so I brought it all the way to the neighborhood and drank it with the feeling of "Do you know this brand?"

Overall, after eating sweet and sour pork and fried rice for breakfast in China, I stopped by Bruda Insa-dong branch, a store that doesn't exist in Gangnam, on my way to a distant town and tried an iced Americano shot. Even though it's not a special coffee, the atmosphere of the store has a certain charm and the prices are good, so I don't think I'll stop by on purpose, but it's worth a stop if you're in the mood for a cup of coffee when you're nearby, so it's delicious.

I visited a friend's painting exhibition in Insa-dong and visited with friends I hadn't seen in a while.
It's been a long time since I've been to Insa-dong, so I was thinking about old times and wandering around wondering which cafe to go to. I ended up going there when I heard that there was a new cafe in a new building with a nice atmosphere.
The name is Sojindam~
It feels like a delicious Korean restaurant rather than a cafe with just the name. The meaning of Sojindam is to contain white treasures.
It is located on the 5th floor and is a rooftop cafe.
It was very spacious both indoors and outdoors and the view was nice.
It was hot so we sat inside and looked outside for a bit.
The drink menu is diverse and the cakes are all homemade.
We ordered the signature lemon cake, black sesame cake, and iced latte.
The price is neither very expensive nor cheap.
The piece of cake seems to be large compared to the price.
The coffee was delicious and the cake was okay and not too spicy.
Perhaps because it was out of town or because it was a weekday afternoon, there weren't many people and we chatted while looking at the view outside the window.
The interior looks clean and pretty~
If you have something to do in Insa-dong, it would be nice to visit at least once.
